title: Rightly Handling the Word
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Rightly handling the Word means treating Scripture faithfully, honestly, and carefully so that its truth is not distorted. God’s Word must not be twisted for pride, control, personal gain, false doctrine, or careless teaching.
summary: Rightly handling the Word means treating Scripture faithfully, honestly, and carefully so that its truth is not distorted. God’s Word must not be twisted for pride, control, personal gain, false doctrine, or careless teaching.
christFocus: Jesus handled Scripture faithfully and resisted Satan’s misuse of it. Rightly handling the Word honors Christ by preserving the truth about His person, Gospel, commands, and saving work.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s Word must be handled with reverence. Scripture is not a tool for manipulation, performance, control, or personal agenda. The one who teaches or uses Scripture must seek to present its meaning faithfully before God.

Rightly handling the Word requires diligence. Believers must pay attention to context, meaning, audience, purpose, and the whole counsel of God. Careless use of Scripture can mislead people even when biblical words are being quoted.

Teachers carry special responsibility. Scripture warns that not many should become teachers because teachers will be judged with greater strictness. Sound doctrine must be taught clearly, and error must be corrected with faithfulness.

The opposite of rightly handling the Word is twisting it. Scripture can be distorted by false teachers, immature readers, or those seeking to justify sin. Faithful handling protects souls and honors the God who spoke.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people have been hurt by Scripture used wrongly. Verses have been pulled out of context to shame, control, silence, exploit, or confuse people. Others have been led into false teaching because Scripture was quoted without being handled truthfully.

This doctrine reminds the church that accuracy is an act of love. Handling Scripture faithfully protects the weak, corrects the wandering, strengthens the church, and keeps the focus on Christ rather than the teacher.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Handle God’s Word with humility and care. Do not quote Scripture to win arguments, excuse sin, impress people, or force your own opinion. Study before you speak. When teaching others, aim to make God’s meaning clear, lead people to Christ, and help them obey the truth.
